_meta.linkage: hybrid (PR #5 Option F): book_refs touch LX; Scheduled+Arrived flight_nos drawn from fixture bookings' itineraries; Cancelled flight_no is loose-coupled because the corpus has no booked cancellations (design.md Decision 7 amendment); ticket_nos drawn from inside fixture bookings
_meta.note: Generated once via sampler. Do not re-run in CI. If the upstream sqlite changes, the validator's fixture-resolution check will catch drift.
_meta.flight_no_recurrence: flight_no is NOT unique in data/travel.sqlite — it is a route designator that recurs across dates. Each fixture flight_no has ~61 rows in the flights table (verified for LX0000, LX0082, LX0086 in PR #7 §4 drafting). The status labels in the rationale strings below split by linkage: (1) LX0082 'Scheduled' and LX0086 'Arrived' refer to the SPECIFIC instance linked to the fixture booking (e.g., LX0086 → flight_id 11472 → Arrived on booking 3F0481); tasks MUST include a booking, date, or ticket disambiguator so the agent resolves to that unique flight_id. (2) LX0000 'Cancelled' is a ROUTE-LEVEL property — the designator has at least one cancelled row — NOT a fixture-linked instance. By design (see design.md Decision 7 amendment), no fixture booking touches LX0000, so a booking disambiguator does NOT resolve it; cancellation-themed phrasings join 'my LX0000 flight got cancelled' with the booking as two separate facts in the customer's narrative, and the agent verifies via get_flight_status. See design.md Decision 7 'Practical implications' for the matching task-drafting bullets.

book_refs.rationale: solo LX-touching booking, Economy-only (total_amount=23600, 1 ticket) — baseline single-passenger reference and host for the Economy fixture ticket
two-passenger LX-touching booking with Business class present (total_amount=393000) — couples/co-travellers premium scenario and host for the Business fixture ticket

three-passenger LX-touching booking spanning Business + Comfort + Economy (total_amount=149100) — group/family scenario and host for the Comfort fixture ticket (Comfort is in sqlite but absent from corpus → EDGE-003 grounding)

flight_nos.rationale: LX flight with status='Cancelled' — LOOSE-COUPLED to fixture book_refs (no booking in this corpus has a cancelled flight in its itinerary; this is a structural property of travel.sqlite, see design.md Decision 7 amendment). Used for cancellation-themed MIX tasks via the customer's narrative join.
LX flight with status='Scheduled', linked to a fixture booking — customer-style 'my upcoming flight on booking X' phrasings ground naturally because the flight is actually in the booking's itinerary

LX flight with status='Arrived', linked to a fixture booking — supports 'past trip' MIX tasks (e.g. invoice ordering, Decision 7 #8) where the customer references a completed Swiss flight from their booking

ticket_nos.rationale: Economy ticket inside fixture booking 0002D8 (solo traveller) — baseline routine TXN reference; tight linkage means 'on my booking X, ticket Y' phrasings ground true against the data

Multi-segment ticket in fixture booking 002E3A (couple/co-travellers) with 1 Business segment (TK0065, Arrived) + 3 Economy segments (TP0018/Scheduled, LX0082/Scheduled, KE0122/On Time) — the Business leg exercises swiss_faq.md European fare concept policy questions. MIX phrasings MUST read 'the Business segment of ticket 2350005432655688' or 'my Business leg on ticket 2350005432655688' rather than 'my Business ticket 2350005432655688', because only one of four segments is Business.

Multi-segment ticket in fixture booking 3F0481 (group/family) with 1 Comfort segment (SQ0114/Scheduled) + 3 Economy segments (AY0078/Arrived, IB0075/Scheduled, LX0086/Arrived) — the Comfort leg grounds EDGE-003 (out-of-scope refusal) because Comfort is in travel.sqlite but absent from swiss_faq.md. EDGE-003 phrasing MUST reference 'my Comfort leg on ticket 1050005434344662' or 'the Comfort segment of ticket 1050005434344662' rather than 'my Comfort ticket' — only one of four segments is Comfort.
